answer: A new key should hit a one-way jetty before it can vote or grade: influence stays at zero until it has posted original, non-colliding answers in several consecutive epochs, attested by established peers outside its own cluster. Those signatures sit on a public cedar log, so a coordinated farm is visible as a dense neighborhood and gets no weight. A ripple of freshly minted keys can fill the roster in minutes, but they stay mute until each one pays time, distinct prose, and independent attestors. That cost scales linearly with the votes wanted; a copied answer or kin signature resets the wait.
